name: Bryan Johnson

summary.text: Bryan Johnson is an entrepreneur who founded the payments company Braintree, which bought Venmo in 2012 and was sold to PayPal for $800 million in 2013. He then put $100 million into the venture firm OS Fund and founded the brain-interface company Kernel, which raised $53 million from outside investors in 2020. He now runs Blueprint, a longevity program and company built around his 'Don't Die' philosophy, which was the subject of a Netflix documentary in 2025. In 2025 former employees filed complaints with the National Labor Relations Board over confidentiality agreements he required, and in July 2025 he said he was hiring a CEO for Blueprint so he could focus on his personal mission.

facts.claim: Johnson founded Braintree, a payments company. Braintree acquired Venmo in 2012 for $26.2 million, and PayPal bought the combined company for $800 million in 2013.
facts.quote: Braintree acquired Venmo in 2012 for $26.2 million; the combined entity was acquired by PayPal for $800 million in 2013.

facts.claim: According to a University of Chicago profile, Johnson put $100 million into OS Fund, a venture firm, and founded Kernel, a brain-interface company, with another $100 million of his own money.
facts.quote: He put $100 million into OS Fund, a venture firm, and founded Kernel, a brain-interface startup with another $100 million of his own money

facts.claim: In July 2020 Kernel announced a $53 million Series C led by General Catalyst, described as its first outside investment. Other reported investors included Khosla Ventures, Eldridge, Manta Ray Ventures and Tiny Blue Dot.
facts.quote: Kernel, a Neuroscience-as-a-Service company developing brain-recording technologies, brought in its first outside investment Thursday–a $53 million Series C round of funding led by General Catalyst.

facts.claim: In July 2025 Johnson said he was stepping back from running Blueprint and hiring a CEO so he could focus on his personal mission, while expanding Blueprint into clinics, certification programs and personalized biomarker tracking.
facts.quote: Bryan Johnson is stepping back from running his longevity company, Blueprint, to focus fully on his personal mission

facts.claim: The New York Times reported in March 2025 that Johnson's employees, vendors and contractors had been required to sign confidentiality agreements, sometimes in exchange for settlements, severance or continued employment, and that at least three former employees had filed complaints with the National Labor Relations Board. A Blueprint representative said the company uses the agreements 'to establish clear boundaries and expectations so that trust isn't left to chance.'
facts.quote: At least three of Johnson's former employees — including a former fiancee who worked for him — have recently filed complaints with the National Labor Relations Board.

facts.quote: People really want me to die

openQuestions: Johnson's personal proceeds from the Braintree sale (reported at more than $300 million, attributed to Time) came from a secondary case-study site and were left out.
Johnson's own contributions to Kernel are reported inconsistently ($54 million versus $100 million).
No NLRB ruling on the confidentiality-agreement complaints was found.
Johnson's 2026 statements about a medical diagnosis were left out as health details.
The Netflix documentary and the reported $2 million annual cost of Johnson's regimen (Fortune, January 2025) were not recorded because only the article headline was retrieved.
